title: Three entry-point docs give three different inventories, all wrong: ARCHITECTURE.md '92 srcs/23 registered, 31 agents, 129 skills' vs README '93 srcs/25 registered, 40+ agents, 137+ skills' vs reality 111 srcs/76 registered, 36 agents, 134 skills

evidence.quote:
| TypeScript hooks | 92 source files, 23 registered | Active in `.claude/hooks/src/` |
| Skills | 129 directories | In `.claude/skills/` |
| Agents | 31 | Defined in `.claude/agents/` |

5. ✅ Installs 40+ specialized agents
6. ✅ Installs 137+ skill workflows
7. ✅ Installs 93 hook source files (25 registered)
<summary>See full agent roster (40+ agents across 9 categories)</summary>

observe_how: Ground truth verified: `ls .claude/hooks/src/*.ts | wc -l` = 111; active settings.json = 76 unique registered; `ls .claude/agents/*.md | wc -l` = 36; sync-architecture-stats.mjs counts 134 SKILL.md dirs. README understates the running hook surface by 3x (25 vs 76) and overstates agents (40+); ARCHITECTURE.md does the inverse (31 agents). Any sizing/triage decision based on these docs starts from a wrong inventory.

title: build/fix/explore workflow chains name four nonexistent skills: research-codebase, test-driven-development, tldr-impact, dependency-preflight

evidence.quote:
"brownfield": ["onboard", "research-codebase", "plan-agent", "validate-agent", "implement_plan"],
    "tdd": ["plan-agent", "test-driven-development", "implement_plan"],
    "refactor": ["tldr-impact", "plan-agent", "test-driven-development", "implement_plan"]

| `deps` | dependency-preflight → oracle → plan-agent → premortem → kraken → qlty-check → commit |
| `pr-comments` | github-search → research-codebase → plan-agent → premortem → kraken → commit |
| **research-codebase** | Pattern documentation (used by deep depth) |

observe_how: ls .claude/skills/ shows actual skill dirs are 'research' (not research-codebase), 'tdd' (not test-driven-development), 'tldr-code' (no tldr-impact skill — impact is a CLI subcommand), and no dependency-preflight skill or agent exists anywhere (.claude/skills/dependency-preflight: No such file; no match in .claude/agents/). These are the literal chain-step identifiers the orchestrator skills instruct the model to 'execute' — each invocation requires the model to guess the real target or fail. /build and /fix are the two primary CLAUDE.md-routed workflows ('implement' → /build, 'bug' → /fix).
causal_links: Skill renames (research-codebase→research, test-driven-development→tdd) were applied to skill dirs during the Phase-4/5 skill evaluation passes but the orchestrator chain definitions that reference them were never updated
